title: Praxis AI — Post-Optimization Savings Draft
executive_summary: Quick working draft showing estimated savings for Praxis AI after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, prefix cache, low-precision quant profile for 7B variant and routing to cheaper region for non-urgent inference). High-level result: ~47% reduction in monthly inference spend under expected traffic profile. This doc is a working artifact intended for internal review and to iterate with Solutions Engineering before sending a customer-facing one-pager.
baseline_workload_snapshot: Representative month (Jan 2025). Traffic: 35M generation tokens + 210M embedding tokens. Traffic pattern: 65% interactive chat requests (p95 latency target 300ms), 35% bulk embedding jobs (batch-friendly). Current model mix: 60% 16B-open variant (hosted), 25% 7B-optimized, 15% 13B for high-quality responses. Current monthly inference cost (customer-reported billing summary): $92,400. Note: baseline includes no request-level batching and embeddings served at on-demand endpoints in us-central1.

assumptions:
- Pricing inputs: current hosted per-token rates as of 2025-01 exported from customer billing sheet.
- Optimized plan uses: (1) Redwood Optimize auto-batching for embeddings (batch size target 512), (2) 7B-lmq quant profile for non-sensitive chat paths, (3) prefix/KV caching for repeat/assistant-context flows.
- No change to application UX except small async fallback for very large embedding jobs.
- Traffic mix and volume remain ~flat over the next 3 months.
- Bandwidth and egress costs excluded from this model (handled by infra team separately).
recommendations: 1) Immediate: enable embedding batching pipeline + move embedding jobs to dedicated batch-optimized endpoint in us-west1. 2) Short term (2–4 weeks): implement model routing rules to prefer 7B-quant for conversational flows where quality delta is acceptable (A/B with 10% traffic). 3) Medium term: deploy prefix/KV cache for top-20 intents and second-turn cached tokens. 4) Ops: add cost/latency alerting per model route and a weekly evaluation sweep for quality regressions tied to our test prompts.
sensitivity_analysis: Low adoption of routing to 7B (10% only) => savings fall to ~$215k/year
Higher-than-expected cache misses (actual hit 15% vs assumed 28%) => savings fall to ~$360k/year
Embedding volume growth +25% with unchanged batching => embedding-specific savings reduce by ~40% relative to projection
next_steps: Confirm redwood-reserved capacity offer for Praxis (quota and burst terms)
Solutions Eng to run a 2-week canary with 10% routing to 7B-quant; collect quality/latency signals
Ask customer to share 30 days of raw request logs for better cache-key modeling (tickets: JIRA-OPT-4123)
Schedule customer review call w/estimate deck (Propose: Feb 28)
questions_for_customer: Are there any regulatory/data residency constraints preventing embeddings from moving to us-west1?
Which 10–20 user intents are highest business value (we can prioritize caching those)
Tolerance for small p50 latency increase if p95 improves?
notes: Working notes: initial bench runs on c6g-like infra show 7B-quant throughput x2.4 vs 16B baseline for same GPU; need to validate in praxis dataset (safety/quality). Drafted numbers assume 30% effective concurrency reduction from batching; we must re-run with live request timing. Tagging Marta for quality evals and Jonas for infra sizing checks.
